headline: Paper reports that emulated NVFP4 pretraining uses more exposures to learn rare facts than BF16
summary: Lu and Zhang's Nov 9 preprint reports that transformer models trained with emulated NVFP4 matrix multiplications need more exposures than BF16 models to reach the same recall on controlled rare facts, even when validation loss is similar. In the primary 40M-parameter comparisons (six seeds), matched-token exposure multipliers are 1.32× for synthetic biographies and 1.52× for a FineWeb-Edu mixture; matched-loss estimates are 1.25× and 1.22×. The authors attribute part of the effect to gradient noise interacting with AdamW. Experiments use emulated FP4 GEMMs on one RTX 4090, models up to 96.6M parameters and up to 1B tokens. Native FP4 throughput, production-scale generalization and independent reproduction are not established.
